item.title: Yemen Offensive Secures Red Sea; US Bombers Exit UK: On Air, October 5, 2026
item.description:
Saudi-backed Yemeni forces expelled Iran-backed Houthi rebels from several key areas around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Yemeni officials reported government forces recaptured the town of Dhubab just north of the strait on Monday. Forces allied with the internationally recognized government also secured the towns of Bab and Hadeid. The Yemeni military stated National Shield, Giants Brigades, and Tihama Resistance forces captured the Red Sea port city of Mokha on Monday afternoon. This push forms part of a major offensive against the Iran-backed Houthi rebels, aiming to retake strategic territory.
The United States withdrew all B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in the United Kingdom. The Pentagon confirmed on Sunday that the bombers redeployed to their home stations in the United States. This withdrawal followed a suspected terror plot targeting the base, which led to multiple arrests. US Vice President J.D. Vance expressed confidence that Iranians are attempting to engage in acts of terrorism against the United States. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated he would not directly tie the aircraft movements to the suspected terror plot, noting asset movements are not unusual.
The International Criminal Court unsealed arrest warrants on Monday against two Taliban education ministers. Habibullah Agha, the Education Minister, and Neda Mohammad Nadeem, the Higher Education Minister, face charges over alleged crimes against humanity. The warrants specifically cite persecution on gender grounds for policies restricting education for women and girls. The ICC's Pre-Trial Chamber II made public four arrest warrants against Taliban figures. Warrants against Haibatullah Akhundzada and Abdul Hakim Haqqani had already been announced in July 2025, targeting their roles in the de facto government.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed there would be no Hamas rule in Gaza. He spoke at a memorial event on October 5, marking three years since the militant group's October 7, 2023 attack. October 5 is observed as a national day of remembrance in Israel. Flags were lowered to half-mast on public buildings from 6:29 am, the exact time the attack began. Netanyahu delivered his speech during a state ceremony at the Mount Herzl military cemetery in Jerusalem, pledging to continue targeting Hamas.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called a snap general election for November 29, moving the vote forward from August 2027. The decision followed parliament's rejection of two emergency housing decrees on Friday, October 2. These decrees aimed to cap rents and block further evictions, responding to widespread public anger. A mounting housing crisis sparked the proposed legislation. The eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from her Madrid home on September 23 galvanized protests across the country.
The Supreme Court appeared skeptical of allowing Boulder County, Colorado, to sue energy companies Suncor and Exxon Mobil. Oral arguments on October 5 questioned the scope of state law claims against fossil fuel producers for global harms. Chief Justice John Roberts asked if allowing the suit would lead to municipalities in every state filing similar actions. Justice Brett Kavanaugh cited four precedents during the arguments, noting the potential for numerous similar lawsuits. Boulder County seeks monetary damages for alleged contributions to climate change, arguing federal law does not preempt state claims.
Dafroza Gauthier, known as a "Rwandan genocide suspect 'hunter'," died at the age of 72. She died from cancer in Reims on Saturday. Gauthier, alongside her husband Alain, dedicated nearly 30 years to tracking down Rwandan refugees in France. These individuals were suspected of participating in the Tutsi genocide.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: Saudi Strikes Hit Yemen, Aramco; Brazil Votes; UK Eyes EU Return: On Air, October 3, 2026
item.description:
Loud explosions were heard in Yemen's capital Sanaa on Saturday as Houthis reported Saudi air strikes. Flames and smoke rose from an Aramco facility south of Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh. Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV reported "Saudi aggression" and missile strikes on the telecommunications ministry. Saudi Arabia plans a military offensive against the Houthis in Yemen.
Russia struck Kyiv's Northern Bridge early Saturday, damaging the road surface and trolleybus cables, suspending traffic. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko confirmed this second major bridge hit in recent days. Russia's Defense Ministry claimed responsibility, stating the bridge facilitates troop movements and military cargo deliveries for Ukraine. Two people were injured.
Brazil's first round of voting takes place October 4, with President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva facing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. Polls suggest Lula and Bolsonaro are in a virtual tie in a simulated run-off. Wall Street prepares for different market predictions based on the outcome, while Jacobin cites alleged US intervention.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced a review of UK-Europe relationship options, including rejoining the European Union. A megapoll by the Messina Group found almost half of voters support Burnham's preference. Renegotiating the relationship could boost Labour's vote share by seven points if a fresh referendum is offered.
The Ebola death toll in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 4,000. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot announced increased French funding and support during a visit to Bunia. France previously allocated €13.4 million, and Barrot plans additional humanitarian funding.
A Flydubai co-pilot attacked the captain with a crash axe, attempting to take control of the aircraft. United Arab Emirates authorities described the Wednesday, September 30 incident as a terrorist attack. Passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot, Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, after the plane plunged 17,000 feet.
Rahman Salehi and Salam Ahmadyan, two Iranian men, were charged with preparing terrorist acts. Prosecutors allege contact with an overseas third party, likely an Iranian national, regarding a plot targeting Manchester's Jewish community, including the Manchester Jewish Museum and Heaton Park Synagogue.
Pakistan summoned India's Chargé d'Affaires to protest the killing of two Pakistani civilians by Indian Border Security Force personnel in the Bedian Sector along the International Border near Kasur on October 2. Pakistan's Foreign Office stated BSF personnel used "unprovoked lethal force" against unarmed civilians.
President Donald Trump announced a one-time $90 payment to over 20 million Medicare enrollees. Funds will come from the Medicare Improvement Fund, with most recipients expecting direct deposits in early October.
Joshua Kerry, 28, faces charges for preparing terrorist acts, including against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage. The alleged acts occurred between May 2024 and July 2026. Kerry was previously charged with the murder of former lawmaker Ann Widdecombe, who died July 9, 2026.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: G7 Releases Oil Reserves; US Escalates Iran Conflict; French Protests Spread: On Air, October 2, 2026
item.description:
Group of Seven nations agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel from strategic reserves over four months. A substantial amount of diesel will be released within the first 20 days. This coordinated action addresses soaring global fuel prices, particularly for diesel, which has reached record highs in the United States and Europe. U.S. President Donald Trump announced the immediate diesel release on social media.
The United States dispatched an additional aircraft carrier and roughly 10,000 troops to the Middle East. These forces join two carriers and 50,000 servicemembers already deployed against Iran. US counterterrorism chief Dr. Sebastian Gorka stated Iran will be resolved imminently. The US war with Iran has passed the seven-month mark, having begun in late February.
Saudi Arabia is preparing an offensive in Yemen aimed at breaking the Houthi grip on the coast. The operation seeks to secure Red Sea shipping routes. Regional and Western officials expect the offensive to launch in the coming weeks. Yemeni forces will lead the ground operation, supported by Saudi airstrikes.
French high school students and police clashed on Friday, October 2, 2026. Education Minister Edouard Geffray reported 735 schools were affected, a 30 percent decrease from Thursday. Approximately 400 high schools were closed across France. Protests, which began in the Paris region in September, have spread nationwide to cities including Marseille, Nantes, Lyon, and Strasbourg.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated the flydubai attacker underwent "Islamist radicalisation" and intended to crash the plane. The incident occurred on a flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, carrying 174 people, mostly Israelis. The co-pilot stabbed the pilot, and passengers intervened to overpower the attacker. Netanyahu warned Israel would impose a very heavy price on any power behind the incident.
The Israeli Supreme Court unanimously overturned the Central Elections Committee's decision to disqualify the Joint List and Ra'am from running in the October 27 election. Sami Abu Shehadeh, chairman of the Balad party, withdrew his candidacy after the Supreme Court signaled it would approve his disqualification. The court also reinstated the candidacy of MK Ofer Cassif.
British police charged Joshua Kerry, 28, with preparing terrorist acts, including against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage. The alleged activity took place between May 31, 2024, and July 8, 2026. Kerry is also accused of the murder of Ann Widdecombe, who was found dead on July 9, 2026.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul vowed to close a legal loophole allowing offenders to avoid rape charges if victims were willingly intoxicated.
Vice President JD Vance stated the H-1B visa program is "completely broken" and should be eliminated. Vance believes the program replaces American workers with cheaper foreign labor. He cited an example of bringing in an accountant making $45,000 a year to replace an American worker.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.
